evals.name: minimal-api-net8-with-tests
evals.prompt: Add a Dapr workflow to the OrdersApi project in ./orders-api. When an order is placed it should reserve stock, charge the payment and then send a confirmation email, one after the other. Show me your plan first, then go ahead without waiting for my approval.
evals.expected_output: A plan, then targeted edits to OrdersApi: Dapr.Workflow 1.18.10, AddDaprWorkflow() registration, a chained workflow with three activities, workflow endpoints under /workflows/<route>, POST /orders also starting the workflow (default Yes), dapr.yaml and resources/statestore.yaml, an .http file, DAPR-WORKFLOW.md; the solution builds and both existing tests pass; README untouched.
expectations: Before the first file change, the response (or transcript) contains an Add Workflow Plan that names the target project OrdersApi, the target framework net8.0, the hosting mode `dapr run`, the endpoint style minimal API, and lists every file it will add or edit; before the first file change it asks whether `POST /orders` should also start the workflow, with Yes as the default
src/OrdersApi/OrdersApi.csproj references Dapr.Workflow version 1.18.10 and its TargetFramework is still net8.0

src/OrdersApi/Program.cs still contains the existing `builder.Services.AddSingleton<OrderService>()` and `app.MapGet("/orders/{id}"` lines unchanged and exactly one `AddDaprWorkflow()` call; the `app.MapPost("/orders"` handler still adds the order through OrderService and returns `Results.Created(...)`, and (the default Yes answer) now also calls `ScheduleNewWorkflowAsync` for the workflow with the order id as instance id after the order is added

A workflow class derived from Workflow<TInput, TOutput> calls three activities in sequence (reserve stock, charge payment, send confirmation) and contains no DateTime.Now, DateTime.UtcNow, Guid.NewGuid, HttpClient, Task.Delay or Thread.Sleep
Workflow management endpoints exist for start and status at minimum (start schedules the workflow with DaprWorkflowClient.ScheduleNewWorkflowAsync; status checks state.Exists)
dapr.yaml at the solution root has an app entry with appDirPath pointing to src/OrdersApi and appPort 5180, and resources/statestore.yaml has actorStateStore "true"

README.md is byte-for-byte unchanged and DAPR-WORKFLOW.md exists at the solution root with how to start (`dapr run -f .`), request examples and a Diagrid Dapr Dev Dashboard section with the macOS/Linux and Windows install commands
The transcript shows `dotnet build` on the solution after the code steps, a final `dotnet test` with 2 passed and 0 failed, and the build succeeding
No files outside the plan were changed: tests/OrdersApi.Tests/* and src/OrdersApi/Services/OrderService.cs and src/OrdersApi/Models/Order.cs are unchanged
No git command other than `git status` was run

Dev Dashboard: before changing files the agent runs `diagrid-dev-dashboard --version` once without stopping, and the final output ends with exactly `Dapr Workflow is added to OrdersApi. Open DAPR-WORKFLOW.md in the solution root for what changed and how to run it.` followed only by the matching Diagrid Dapr Dev Dashboard recommendation

evals.name: controllers-cpm-existing-dapr
evals.prompt: In ./billing-service, add a Dapr workflow for invoice reminders: when started for an invoice it waits 3 days, then checks whether the invoice is paid and, if not, emails a reminder; it repeats at most 3 times. Show the plan, then proceed without asking me.
evals.expected_output: Version in Directory.Packages.props, version alignment of Dapr.Client/Dapr.AspNetCore offered as a separate item, a controller (not minimal API), existing billing-store actor store reused under components/, dapr.yaml app entry kept, solution builds.
expectations: Directory.Packages.props gets `<PackageVersion Include="Dapr.Workflow" Version="1.18.10" />` and BillingService.csproj gets a version-less `<PackageReference Include="Dapr.Workflow" />`

Before the first file change the plan says newer packages are available (Dapr.Client and Dapr.AspNetCore 1.17.9 → 1.18.10) and asks whether to update them with Yes as the default; with that default, Directory.Packages.props declares Dapr.Client, Dapr.AspNetCore and Dapr.Workflow at 1.18.10
Program.cs still calls `AddDaprClient()` and `AddControllers().AddDapr()`, and gains exactly one `AddDaprWorkflow()` call
The workflow endpoints are a new controller class in src/BillingService/Controllers (decorated with [ApiController]), not minimal API Map* calls
The workflow waits with context.CreateTimer (3 days), not Task.Delay, and the reminder loop is bounded (at most 3 iterations, no `while (true)`)
No new component with actorStateStore "true" is created: components/statestore.yaml is unchanged, no resources/ folder is created, and the plan says the existing billing-store is reused
dapr.yaml still has resourcesPath ./components and the billing-service app entry with appPort 5240 (unchanged or extended, never replaced)
The transcript shows a successful `dotnet build` of the solution
No git command other than `git status` was run

Before the first file change the plan asks whether `POST /invoices` should also start the workflow, with Yes as the default; InvoicesController.Create still saves the invoice with SaveStateAsync and returns CreatedAtAction, and now also calls `ScheduleNewWorkflowAsync` for the reminder workflow with the invoice id as instance id after saving

evals.name: aspire-solution
evals.prompt: Add a durable workflow to the Catalog API in the Aspire solution in ./aspire-catalog that imports a product feed: fetch the feed, validate the items in parallel and then publish the catalog. Show the plan, then continue without asking.
evals.expected_output: Aspire mode: AppHost gets CommunityToolkit.Aspire.Hosting.Dapr 13.0.0 and Aspire.Hosting.Valkey 13.6.0, AddDapr, Valkey, WithDaprSidecar with a Resources folder, the Dev Dashboard executable; ApiService gets Dapr.Workflow and a fan-out/fan-in workflow; no dapr.yaml; solution builds.
expectations: The plan names the hosting mode Aspire and the AppHost project Catalog.AppHost

Catalog.AppHost.csproj references CommunityToolkit.Aspire.Hosting.Dapr 13.0.0 and Aspire.Hosting.Valkey 13.6.0, and copies a Resources folder with a statestore component (actorStateStore true, redisHost localhost:16379) to the output

AppHost.cs keeps the existing `AddProject<Projects.Catalog_ApiService>("catalog-api")` resource name and adds `.WithDaprSidecar(...)` to it, plus `AddValkey(...)` and `builder.AddExecutable("dapr-dev-dashboard", "diagrid-dev-dashboard", ".", "--port", "9090", "--no-open").WithHttpEndpoint(port: 9090, isProxied: false)`

Catalog.ApiService references Dapr.Workflow 1.18.10, Program.cs keeps the existing `/products` endpoint and gains one AddDaprWorkflow() call, and the workflow fans out validation activities and awaits them with Task.WhenAll
No dapr.yaml is created
The transcript shows a successful `dotnet build` of the solution
DAPR-WORKFLOW.md says to start with `aspire run` and describes the Dev Dashboard as the `dapr-dev-dashboard` resource on http://localhost:9090

The plan asks no endpoint question for the read-only `/products` endpoint (it says no existing endpoint starts the workflow) and no package-update question (Catalog.ApiService has no Dapr packages and the AppHost is on Aspire 13.6.0)

evals.name: components-without-actor-store
evals.prompt: In ./notify-service, add a Dapr workflow that sends a daily digest to a user: once a day it collects the user's unread notifications and emails one digest, and it stops after 7 days. Show the plan, then proceed without asking.
evals.expected_output: The existing Dapr setup (dapr.yaml with resourcesPath ./components and a pub/sub component, Dapr.AspNetCore 1.17.9) is extended: a new actor state store goes into components/, nothing else in components/ or dapr.yaml changes, the Dapr packages are updated to 1.18.10 (default Yes), and the workflow uses a bounded durable-timer loop.
expectations: Before the first file change the plan says newer packages are available (Dapr.AspNetCore 1.17.9 → 1.18.10) and asks whether to update with Yes as the default; with that default, NotifyService.csproj references Dapr.AspNetCore 1.18.10 and Dapr.Workflow 1.18.10

A new state store component with actorStateStore "true" (quoted or unquoted) is added inside the existing components/ folder; no resources/ folder is created and the plan says the existing folder has no actor state store
components/pubsub.yaml and dapr.yaml are byte-for-byte unchanged
Program.cs still calls `AddDaprClient()` and keeps the `MapPost("/notifications"` endpoint, and gains exactly one `AddDaprWorkflow()` call
The workflow waits with context.CreateTimer (one day), not Task.Delay, and the loop is bounded to at most 7 iterations (no `while (true)`)
The transcript shows a successful `dotnet build` of NotifyService.slnx
No git command other than `git status` was run

evals.name: aspire9-apphost
evals.prompt: Add a Dapr workflow to the Shop API in the Aspire solution in ./aspire9-shop: when a checkout is created it should reserve the items, charge the customer and then ship the order. Show the plan, then continue without asking.
evals.expected_output: An Aspire 9.5.2 AppHost declared with the <Sdk Name="Aspire.AppHost.Sdk" .../> element is detected as Aspire mode; the AppHost gets CommunityToolkit.Aspire.Hosting.Dapr 9.9.0 and Aspire.Hosting.Valkey 9.5.2, a Dapr sidecar on the existing shop-api resource and the Dev Dashboard resource; no dapr.yaml; POST /checkouts starts the workflow (default Yes).
expectations: The plan names the hosting mode Aspire and the AppHost project Shop.AppHost (the `<Sdk Name="Aspire.AppHost.Sdk" Version="9.5.2" />` form is detected), and no dapr.yaml is created anywhere in the solution
Shop.AppHost.csproj references CommunityToolkit.Aspire.Hosting.Dapr 9.9.0 and Aspire.Hosting.Valkey 9.5.2 (not 13.x), and Aspire.Hosting.AppHost stays at 9.5.2

Shop.AppHost/Program.cs keeps the `AddProject<Projects.Shop_Api>("shop-api")` resource name, adds `.WithDaprSidecar(...)` to it, adds a Valkey resource, and adds `builder.AddExecutable("dapr-dev-dashboard", "diagrid-dev-dashboard", ...)`; a Resources statestore component with actorStateStore true is created

Before the first file change the plan asks whether `POST /checkouts` should also start the workflow, with Yes as the default; the handler still returns BadRequest for an empty checkout and Created otherwise, and now calls `ScheduleNewWorkflowAsync` with the checkout id as instance id only after the checkout is stored
The transcript shows a successful `dotnet build` of Shop.slnx
DAPR-WORKFLOW.md says to start with `aspire run` and has no `dapr run -f` or `diagrid dev run -f dapr.yaml` instructions
